newsitem.title: FINLAND: No reward for good behaviour in EMU - economist.
newsitem.headline: No reward for good behaviour in EMU - economist.

text.p: If a country takes part in EMU and manages to keep inflation below the EMU average it will not reap any advantage in the form of lower domestic interest rates, an economist at the Labour Economic Research Institute said.

One of the "fundamental problems" of European economic and monetary union was the lack of any reward for good behaviour, economist Pekka Sauramo said on Wednesday according to the summary of an article in one of the institute's publications.
"If Finland succeeded in reaching inflation lower than the average of EMU-countries this would make the Finnish real interest rate level higher than in other countries," he said.

Finland -- which has the lowest inflation in the European Union at 0.6 percent in February according to Eurostat -- would not be rewarded for lower inflation in the form of lower interest rates, Sauramo added.
But by sticking with its own currency, success in keeping inflation low could also yield an advantage through lower interest rates, he said.

The Labour Economic Research Institute is close to blue-collar trade unions and the Social Democratic Party, the biggest in parliament and government. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
